title: 10 Habits That Make Adulthood Feel Less Exhausting
author: Antonius Veritas
summary: Writing as a physician and Stoic practitioner, Antonius Veritas argues that adulthood feels like a scam because people sacrifice the very pleasures and habits that give them the energy for everything else. He offers ten habits grounded in the Stoics: give days structure, as Seneca urged on the shortness of life; build a strong body, as Cato did; read good books; stop resisting what happens, following Epictetus; deal with problems while they are small; learn to disappoint people; make time for loved ones; learn to enjoy your own company, as Marcus Aurelius did in his Meditations; make room for what you love; and work toward a life with more freedom. A recurring thread is that how we do one thing is how we do everything, so habits of follow-through and discipline spread through character. He insists that Stoicism is not merely endurance but a philosophy for living well through wisdom, courage, justice and temperance. The essay mixes personal anecdotes from medical school with classical sources and ends with an invitation to subscribe.
points: The things adults sacrifice, such as exercise, friendship and pleasure, are often the sources of the energy needed to handle their responsibilities.
Structuring days with a plan gives people somewhere to return when life interrupts and ensures exercise, reading, friends and rest are not left to leftover time.
Dealing with problems while they are small prevents misunderstandings becoming resentment and trains the character to follow through when tasks are unpleasant.
Learning to disappoint people is framed as a Stoic boundary: we can advise and help, but other people's judgments and choices belong to them.
Stoicism is presented as a philosophy of living well, not just tolerating hardship, aimed at building a life with more freedom.
quotes: We forget that the whole point of earning a living is to have a life worth living.
Seneca observed that people will defend their property fiercely, yet allow others to take up their time without much resistance.
Once we make room for exercise, reading, friends, and rest in our schedules, we no longer have to depend on having time left over after everything else is done.
When you become accustomed to running, walking feels easier. When you learn to run faster, the pace that once exhausted you becomes more manageable.
It means recognizing that once something has happened, no amount of complaining can undo it. In fact, whining just makes things harder. We still have to decide what comes next.
The idea that helped me was simple- how I do one thing is how I do everything.
But kindness doesn’t require us to abandon our own responsibilities, and love doesn’t give us authority over another person’s choices.
They forget that its purpose is to help you live well, to develop the wisdom, courage, justice, and temperance that make a flourishing life possible.
